role: Tier 2 speech assembly engine that constructs sentences from knowledge graph data without LLM involvement.
detail: SentenceAssembler class resolves graph node bindings to natural English sentences using ConversationPattern templates with 8 built-in patterns (state_fact_copular, ask_what_is, state_has_property, confirm_understanding, admit_ignorance, describe_count, greet_response, ask_to_teach). Core pipeline: pattern lookup -> slot resolution with grammatical role checking -> English grammar application (articles via vowel detection on _VOWELS frozenset) -> template interpolation. find_speakable_facts queries IS_A edges (min_confidence 0.5), HAS_PROPERTY edges (min_confidence 0.5), and low-degree WordSenseNode nodes. All exceptions in assemble() return None for fallback to Tier 1 (LLM speech). Slot resolution checks node.properties for spelling, name, or label_raw fields. Graph queries iterate up to limit*2 then cap at limit.
gotchas: Article heuristic uses only vowel-initial detection, acknowledged insufficient for edge cases (a unicorn, an hour); TODO in docstring notes this. find_teachable_topics counts outgoing edges naively (no threshold), marks degree<=1 as teachable with confidence 0.3 (hardcoded). Graph query results capped by slicing [:limit*2] then [:limit], no pagination. Exception handling in assemble catches all and logs warning, never raises. Missing bindings return None silently. No graph mutation, all read-only. Async throughout.
